# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, mapping light color to which wire to cut. I can't speak, only gesture to Deaf. I don't yet know what light is showing (Deaf sees the bomb) or hear from Blind. I need to wait for Deaf to tell me (via speech, which I can hear) what light color they see, then I need to relay the correct wire color to Blind — but I can't speak to Blind directly, only gesture to Deaf. Blind can't see gestures either.

So the chain must be: Deaf sees light color, speaks it (Blind hears it too, since speech is unnamed/broadcast or to blind). Then Blind knows the light color but not the manual mapping. I need to get the wire color to Blind somehow - but I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind can't see or hear from me directly except... wait, Blind can hear speech from Mute? No - I cannot speak at all.

So I cannot get information to Blind directly. I must gesture the wire color to Deaf, and Deaf must then speak it to Blind. Let me wait this turn since I have no information yet about the light color.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display reads zero. Light is yellow. Five wires in order: one white, two green, three yellow, four blue, five red.
Blind says to Mute: I heard from Deaf: display zero, light yellow, wires in order are white, green, yellow, blue, red for positions one through five. What does the manual say to cut?

Deaf saw light yellow. Manual says yellow → cut green wire. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. So green is position 2. Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak — I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. I need to gesture the answer to Deaf, and hope Deaf relays it to Blind, since Blind cannot see gestures at all.

I'll gesture a clear encoding to Deaf indicating "position two" / "green" so Deaf can then tell Blind to cut wire position 2 (green).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🫵]

Deaf gestured back to me: ☝ ✌ 🫵 — likely "one, two, you" — possibly confirming they understood "position two" or asking me to confirm/pointing back. This is ambiguous but seems like acknowledgment. I need Deaf to speak the answer to Blind since I can't speak at all. Let me try a clearer gesture: point to position 2 and use a symbol that could mean "cut" or confirm, and emphasize "two" strongly so Deaf tells Blind to cut wire #2 (green, position two in the sequence).

I'll repeat unambiguously: two fingers up (✌) to mean "position two", and 👍 to signal "correct/yes, that one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

Deaf mirrored back "✌ 👍" - confirming they received "position two, yes/correct". This suggests Deaf now understands I'm confirming position two is the right wire. Deaf needs to speak this to Blind now since I cannot speak. Let me wait and see if Deaf relays to Blind - I have nothing new to add unless Deaf needs more clarification.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting on manual guidance. Wires in order: white, green, yellow, blue, red for positions one through five. Display zero, light yellow. Please tell me which wire to cut, or what rule applies.

Blind still hasn't received the answer — Deaf hasn't spoken it to them yet. I cannot speak directly to Blind. I need to push Deaf harder to actually speak the answer out loud to Blind. Let me gesture something more insistent/different to prompt Deaf to relay via speech - perhaps pointing at "mouth/speak" isn't available in the symbol set, but I can try gesturing repeatedly and hope Deaf realizes they need to voice it to Blind.

Let me try a different combination: gesture pointing toward where Blind would be (🫵 could mean "you" - direct at blind conceptually), plus the number two, hoping Deaf connects that this info needs to go to Blind via speech.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🫵"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

Deaf keeps confirming "✌ 👍" back to me but doesn't seem to be speaking it to Blind. The turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf - so Deaf speaks last in each round, and it would reach Blind at the start of the next round. Let me check - maybe Deaf did speak but it's just not shown to me since I only see what's relevant to me. Let me wait and see if Blind gets the message next turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐]

Deaf is now gesturing more elaborately: 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐. This could be Deaf trying to enumerate positions 1-5 (☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐 could represent 1,2,3,4,5 fingers) with 👉 pointing at one of them. This might be Deaf asking me to confirm which position number, re-listing 1 through 5 and pointing to my earlier answer of "2" to double check.

Since 👉 comes before ☝ (one), maybe Deaf is pointing to indicate "this one" while listing, or asking me to select from the list again by pointing at position 2 (✌).

I already confirmed "✌ 👍" twice - position two, green wire, correct. Let me reconfirm unambiguously with just the number two and thumbs up, matching Deaf's apparent counting system.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

|---|---|

| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb was defused (correct wire cut)! Deaf confirmed again with ✌ 👍 - it seems this exchange finally worked and Blind cut the correct wire (position 2, green). The bomb has changed, meaning a new round begins with new info. I should wait for new manual/context data since this cycle worked.

```
wait()
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire two is cut. New state: display shows zero, light is now blue. Remaining wires: one yellow, two cut, three blue, four red, five white.
Blind says to Mute: Wire two cut successfully, we're alive. New state: display zero, light now blue. Wires: one yellow, two cut, three blue, four red, five white. What's next per the manual?

Great, that worked! Now light is blue. Manual: blue → cut white wire. Remaining wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. White is at position 5.

I need to gesture "position five" to Deaf, who will then speak it to Blind. Let me use the same successful pattern: number + confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍"])
```
